thread:
maya: FYI support ticket from AcmeCorp — sudden p99 spike on /v1/generate using model-redwood/large-2025 on prod-us-west. Customer sees p99 ~6s up from ~450ms. They attached recent logs showing repeated OOMs and long GC pauses.

raj: copying in metrics — getting the grafana snapshot now. @maya do we have which shard / worker group this hit?

maya: their request_id: r-0a1b2c3d. Looks like traffic routed to shard rwd-usw-3 (gpu-pool-12). I can share logs:

maya: ```
[2029-03-27T14:02:13Z] ERROR worker: alloc failed: OOM when allocating 2147483648 bytes
[2029-03-27T14:02:13Z] WARN worker: kv_cache_size=13.7GB kv_entries=1.2M seq_len=8192 live_tensors=884 
[2029-03-27T14:02:13Z] INFO worker: fallback to cpu (slow path)
```

ben: seq_len=8192 for a request? that's huge. Is this a streaming/chat session with unbounded KV growth?

emily: customer says they stream long chat histories for a cohort of users, looks like a couple sessions blew past the typical token limits. They filed an SLA escal.

raj: timeline: p95 was OK, p99 drifted first at 13:40 then steady. I see GPU memory fragmentation metrics: per-GPU free chunks small, high external fragmentation. KV cache growth correlates with the long sessions.

raj: immediate mitigation options: (1) evict KV aggressively on that shard, (2) restart affected workers to release fragmented allocations, (3) temporarily route traffic off gpu-pool-12, (4) apply per-tenant max_seq_len at routing.

maya: can we do a rolling canary restart on rwd-usw-3? We should avoid full pool restart. Also want to test a worker with `KV_EVICT_RATIO=0.7` first.

deploy-bot: @maya acknowledged. Initiating canary restart of deploy/model-worker@rwd-usw-3 (1/20) — watch logs for OOMs.

oncall-bot: Paging @raj and @ben — oncall policy triggered: high p99 latency for model-redwood/large-2025 in prod-us-west.

raj: running quick query to list kv sizes per-shard:

raj: ```
select shard, sum(kv_bytes) as bytes from runtime.kv_stats where ts > now() - 1h group by shard order by bytes desc limit 10;
-- result: rwd-usw-3: 13.7GB, rwd-usw-7: 2.1GB, ...
```

ben: that 13.7GB is abnormal for that model; normal is ~1–2GB. Likely leak or unbounded per-session accumulation. Also allocator hist shows many medium-sized chunks leaked (~64–512KB). Jemalloc fragmentation looks bad.

raj: short playbook I suggest:
- step 1: canary restart one worker in rwd-usw-3 with `MALLOC_CONF: "dirty_decay_ms:15000,muzzy_decay_ms:15000,lg_dirty_mult:16"` to trigger faster purging.
- step 2: enable `KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.6` on that canary.
- step 3: monitor p99 and GPU free-chunks for 10m.

maya: I'm doing step 1+2 now. Pushing env and restarting one replica. Will keep canary in service and redirect 5% of traffic to it.

deploy-bot: Canary restart complete (worker-9). Restart logs: ```released 14.1GB pages, reclaimed 11.9GB, kv_evicted=420k entries```. Health checks passed.

raj: checking metrics — after canary restart p99 on canary route down to 620ms from 6s. Non-canary still bad. Good sign.

emily: I told AcmeCorp we started mitigations and expect improvement. They asked for repro steps and root cause hypothesis.

ben: hypothesis: long chat streaming allows unbounded KV growth (we store prefix KV per turn). Two compounding factors: (a) per-request allowed seq_len default is 8192 for that tenant via legacy override, (b) allocator fragmentation prevents timely reclaim so OOMs happen even when nominal free memory exists.

raj: longer term fixes:
- enforce per-tenant hard cap on seq_len at the routing layer (e.g., 4096 default, with opt-in higher via contract),
- add periodic KV compaction job per-shard to trim inactive session prefixes,
- improve allocator configs and consider switching to tcmalloc on these GPUs where fragmentation shows worst P99,
- add telemetry alert: `kv_bytes_per_shard > 5GB for 5m` and `gpu_free_frag_ratio < 0.12` to warn before p99 regression.

maya: immediate follow-up actions documented and assigned:
- raj -> create alert and run a rolling restart plan for rwd-usw-3 (priority)
- ben -> prototype per-request kv cap and eviction heuristics (short-term patch)
- emily -> update customer with interim mitigation and ETA for root cause fix

emily: updated AcmeCorp: "we performed a canary restart and enabled temporary aggressive KV eviction; you should see p99 improvements within minutes. We're implementing routing caps to prevent recurrence and will follow up with a postmortem."

raj: ran rolling restart on remaining 19 replicas with stagger 30s. Observed reclaimed memory per worker ~10–13GB. Cluster p99 dropped to ~480ms overall after restarts and eviction.

emily: Customer confirms degraded calls dropped from 0.9% to 0.02%, they are happy for now but asked for postmortem and permanent fix.

ben: follow-up engineering tasks:
- add per-request KV cap in runtime (config flag `max_kv_entries_per_request`, default 10000),
- add a compaction/defrag endpoint so operators can trigger lightweight compaction without a restart,
- tune jemalloc defaults in the base image and test on perf infra,
- add unit/integration tests that simulate long streaming sessions to catch regressions.

maya: tagging this for postmortem. I'll create the incident doc and link logs + grafana snapshots. Also recommend we ship a short-term config change to routing to deny seq_len > 4096 unless tenant has explicit quota.

raj: created alert PR and scheduled a small rollback-safe rollout for the new jemalloc config on a canary pool next week.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2034, severity 2. Assigned: raj, ben, maya.

maya: closing loop here — marking as "triaged". Will follow up with a postmortem and customer-facing summary once we have root cause confirmed.

emily: thanks all. Customer will keep this ticket open for the PM follow-up.

ben: note for postmortem: add a reproducible script that fires a stable client to stream >100k tokens to reproduce KV growth and fragmentation locally.

maya: good call. I'll add that to the incident doc.

raj: nice job team. Learned: aggressive KV caching is great for latency until per-request work goes unbounded. Need guardrails.

emily: update — customer sent a thumbs up :thumbsup: and asked for weekly updates until permanent fix is deployed.

maya: end.
